items.good: By the time we reached the station, the last train had already left.
items.ko: 우리가 역에 도착했을 즈음 마지막 열차는 이미 떠난 뒤였어요.
bad: By the time we reached the station, the last train has already left.
By the time we reached the station, the last train already leaves.
By the time we reached the station, the last train will already left.

cz.st: By the time we reached the station, the last train ___ already left.

items.rule: 기준이 되는 과거 시점보다 먼저 끝난 일은 had + p.p.(과거완료)로 나타내요.
items.hint: 기준 시점이 과거인지 현재인지 먼저 보세요.

items.good: She has lived in Busan since she was a child.
items.ko: 그녀는 어릴 때부터 부산에서 살아 왔어요.
bad: She lives in Busan since she was a child.
She has lived in Busan for she was a child.
She is living in Busan since she was a child.

cz.st: She ___ lived in Busan since she was a child.

items.rule: 과거에 시작해 지금까지 이어지는 상태는 have/has + p.p.로 쓰고, 시작 시점 앞에는 since를 써요.

items.good: They have been waiting for the bus for almost forty minutes.
items.ko: 그들은 거의 40분 동안 버스를 기다리고 있어요.
bad: They have been wait for the bus for almost forty minutes.
They has been waiting for the bus for almost forty minutes.
They have being waiting for the bus for almost forty minutes.

cz.st: They have ___ waiting for the bus for almost forty minutes.

items.rule: 현재완료진행은 have/has been + -ing 형태예요.

items.good: I haven't seen Minjun since last Friday.
items.ko: 나는 지난 금요일 이후로 민준이를 보지 못했어요.
bad: I didn't see Minjun since last Friday.
I haven't seen Minjun for last Friday.
I'm not seeing Minjun since last Friday.

cz.st: I haven't ___ Minjun since last Friday.

items.rule: '~ 이후로 계속 ~하지 못했다'는 since와 함께 현재완료 부정(haven't + p.p.)을 써요. see의 p.p.는 seen이에요.

items.good: How long have you known your best friend?
items.ko: 너는 가장 친한 친구를 안 지 얼마나 됐니?
bad: How long do you know your best friend?
How long have you knew your best friend?
How long are you knowing your best friend?

cz.st: How long have you ___ your best friend?

items.rule: know 같은 상태 동사는 진행형을 쓰지 않고 현재완료(have + p.p.)로 '얼마 동안'을 물어요.

items.good: We have been friends for more than ten years.
items.ko: 우리는 10년 넘게 친구로 지내 왔어요.
bad: We have been friends since more than ten years.
We are friends for more than ten years.
We have been friends during more than ten years.

cz.st: We have been friends ___ more than ten years.

items.rule: 기간(ten years)에는 for, 시작 시점에는 since를 써요.

items.good: Mr. Han has gone to Jeju, so he isn't here now.
items.ko: 한 선생님은 제주에 가셨어요, 그래서 지금 여기에 안 계세요.
bad: Mr. Han has been to Jeju, so he isn't here now.
Mr. Han have gone to Jeju, so he isn't here now.
Mr. Han has go to Jeju, so he isn't here now.

cz.st: Mr. Han has ___ to Jeju, so he isn't here now.

items.rule: has gone to는 '가고 없다(아직 돌아오지 않음)', has been to는 '다녀온 적이 있다(지금은 돌아옴)'를 뜻해요.

items.good: I have never tried skiing, so I am a little nervous.
items.ko: 나는 스키를 한 번도 타 본 적이 없어서 조금 긴장돼요.
bad: I have ever tried skiing, so I am a little nervous.
I have never try skiing, so I am a little nervous.
I has never tried skiing, so I am a little nervous.

cz.st: I have ___ tried skiing, so I am a little nervous.

items.rule: 경험이 전혀 없음은 have never + p.p.로 말해요. 평서문 긍정문에서 ever는 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Have you finished your homework yet?
items.ko: 너는 숙제를 벌써 끝냈니?
bad: Have you finish your homework yet?
Do you finished your homework yet?
Has you finished your homework yet?

cz.st: Have you ___ your homework yet?

items.rule: 의문문의 yet은 '이미(벌써) 했는지'를 묻고, 현재완료(have + 주어 + p.p.) 어순을 써요.

items.good: The company has increased its sales by twenty percent this year.
items.ko: 그 회사는 올해 매출을 20퍼센트 늘렸어요.
bad: The company has increase its sales by twenty percent this year.
The company is increased its sales by twenty percent this year.
The company has increasing its sales by twenty percent this year.

cz.st: The company has ___ its sales by twenty percent this year.

items.rule: this year처럼 아직 끝나지 않은 기간의 결과는 현재완료(has + p.p.)로 말해요.

items.good: I lost my wallet yesterday, and I still haven't found it.
items.ko: 나는 어제 지갑을 잃어버렸고, 아직도 찾지 못했어요.
bad: I have lost my wallet yesterday, and I still haven't found it.
I lose my wallet yesterday, and I still haven't found it.
I was lost my wallet yesterday, and I still haven't found it.

cz.st: I ___ my wallet yesterday, and I still haven't found it.

items.rule: yesterday처럼 과거의 한 시점을 나타내는 말과는 현재완료가 아니라 과거시제를 써요.

items.good: She went to Paris in 2019, and she has wanted to go back ever since.
items.ko: 그녀는 2019년에 파리에 갔고, 그 이후로 줄곧 다시 가고 싶어 했어요.
bad: She has gone to Paris in 2019, and she has wanted to go back ever since.
She went to Paris in 2019, and she wants to go back ever since.
She goes to Paris in 2019, and she has wanted to go back ever since.

cz.st: She went to Paris in 2019, and she has ___ to go back ever since.

items.rule: 과거의 한 시점(in 2019)은 과거시제, 그 후 지금까지 이어지는 마음은 현재완료로 써요.

items.good: When did you move to this city?
items.ko: 너는 이 도시로 언제 이사 왔니?
bad: When have you moved to this city?
When do you moved to this city?
When did you moved to this city?

cz.st: When ___ you move to this city?

items.rule: when으로 시점을 직접 물을 때는 현재완료가 아니라 과거시제 의문문(did + 주어 + 동사원형)을 써요.

items.good: After he had finished his dinner, he went out for a walk.
items.ko: 그는 저녁을 다 먹은 뒤 산책하러 나갔어요.
bad: After he has finished his dinner, he went out for a walk.
After he had finish his dinner, he went out for a walk.
After he finishing his dinner, he went out for a walk.

cz.st: After he ___ finished his dinner, he went out for a walk.

items.rule: 과거에 일어난 두 일 가운데 먼저 일어난 일은 had + p.p.로 나타내요.

items.good: The movie had already started when we got to the cinema.
items.ko: 우리가 영화관에 도착했을 때 영화는 이미 시작되어 있었어요.
bad: The movie has already started when we got to the cinema.
The movie had already starting when we got to the cinema.
The movie have already started when we got to the cinema.

cz.st: The movie had already ___ when we got to the cinema.

items.rule: 과거의 어느 시점에 이미 완료된 일은 had + p.p.예요.

items.good: I was tired because I had stayed up until three the night before.
items.ko: 나는 전날 밤 세 시까지 깨어 있었기 때문에 피곤했어요.
bad: I was tired because I have stayed up until three the night before.
I was tired because I am staying up until three the night before.
I was tired because I had stay up until three the night before.

cz.st: I was tired because I ___ stayed up until three the night before.

items.rule: 과거의 결과(was tired)보다 앞선 원인은 had + p.p.로 나타내요.

items.good: He noticed that he had left his umbrella on the bus.
items.ko: 그는 우산을 버스에 두고 내렸다는 것을 알아차렸어요.
bad: He noticed that he had leave his umbrella on the bus.
He noticed that he had leaved his umbrella on the bus.
He noticed that he has leaved his umbrella on the bus.

cz.st: He noticed that he had ___ his umbrella on the bus.

items.rule: leave의 과거분사는 left예요. 불규칙 동사는 p.p. 형태를 따로 외워야 해요.

items.good: By next June, I will have saved enough money for the trip.
items.ko: 내년 6월쯤이면 나는 여행에 쓸 돈을 충분히 모아 놓았을 거예요.
bad: By next June, I have saved enough money for the trip.
By next June, I will have save enough money for the trip.
By next June, I will had saved enough money for the trip.

cz.st: By next June, I will ___ saved enough money for the trip.

items.rule: 미래의 한 시점까지 완료될 일은 will have + p.p.(미래완료)로 나타내요.

items.good: By the time you arrive, we will have finished dinner.
items.ko: 네가 도착할 즈음이면 우리는 저녁을 다 먹었을 거예요.
bad: By the time you will arrive, we will have finished dinner.
By the time you arrive, we will finished dinner.
By the time you arrived, we will have finished dinner.

cz.st: By the time you ___, we will have finished dinner.

items.rule: 시간을 나타내는 by the time 절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제로 써요.
items.hint: 시간 접속사 뒤의 동사 형태를 떠올려 보세요.

items.good: She will have worked at the hospital for ten years next month.
items.ko: 다음 달이면 그녀는 그 병원에서 10년째 일하게 돼요.
bad: She will has worked at the hospital for ten years next month.
She will have work at the hospital for ten years next month.
She will worked at the hospital for ten years next month.

cz.st: She will have ___ at the hospital for ten years next month.

items.rule: will have + p.p.는 미래의 한 시점까지의 완료나 계속을 나타내요. will 뒤에는 has가 아니라 have가 와요.

items.good: It has been raining since early morning, so the ground is wet.
items.ko: 이른 아침부터 비가 오고 있어서 땅이 젖어 있어요.
bad: It is raining since early morning, so the ground is wet.
It has been rain since early morning, so the ground is wet.
It has raining since early morning, so the ground is wet.

cz.st: It has been ___ since early morning, so the ground is wet.

items.rule: 지금까지 계속 이어지는 동작을 강조할 때는 have/has been + -ing를 써요.

items.good: I have been learning the guitar for six months now.
items.ko: 나는 지금까지 6개월째 기타를 배우고 있어요.
bad: I learn the guitar for six months now.
I have been learn the guitar for six months now.
I am being learning the guitar for six months now.

cz.st: I have been ___ the guitar for six months now.

items.rule: '지금까지 ~ 동안 ~해 오고 있다'는 have been + -ing와 for로 나타내요.

items.good: I have known Ms. Park since I was in middle school.
items.ko: 나는 중학교 때부터 박 선생님을 알아 왔어요.
bad: I have been knowing Ms. Park since I was in middle school.
I am knowing Ms. Park since I was in middle school.
I know Ms. Park since I was in middle school.

cz.st: I have ___ Ms. Park since I was in middle school.

items.rule: know는 상태를 나타내는 동사라 진행형(-ing)으로 쓰지 않고 현재완료(have known)로 써요.

items.good: How long have you been standing here?
items.ko: 너는 여기에 얼마나 오래 서 있었니?
bad: How long have you stand here?
How long are you standing here since?
How long did you been standing here?

cz.st: How long have you been ___ here?

items.rule: How long ~?에 동작이 계속된 시간을 묻는 말은 have you been + -ing 형태예요.

items.good: He is out of breath because he has just run up the stairs.
items.ko: 그는 방금 계단을 뛰어 올라와서 숨이 차요.
bad: He is out of breath because he has just ran up the stairs.
He is out of breath because he is just ran up the stairs.
He is out of breath because he has just runs up the stairs.

cz.st: He is out of breath because he has just ___ up the stairs.

items.rule: run은 run-ran-run으로 변해요. 현재완료에는 과거형 ran이 아니라 p.p. run이 와요.

items.good: My brother has broken his leg, so he can't play soccer.
items.ko: 내 동생은 다리가 부러져서 축구를 할 수 없어요.
bad: My brother has broke his leg, so he can't play soccer.
My brother is broken his leg, so he can't play soccer.
My brother has breaking his leg, so he can't play soccer.

cz.st: My brother has ___ his leg, so he can't play soccer.

items.rule: 현재 상황의 원인이 되는 과거의 일은 현재완료로 말해요. break의 p.p.는 broken이에요.

items.good: I had never flown before, so I was excited about the trip.
items.ko: 나는 전에 비행기를 타 본 적이 없어서 여행에 들떠 있었어요.
bad: I had never flew before, so I was excited about the trip.
I had never fly before, so I was excited about the trip.
I have never flew before, so I was excited about the trip.

cz.st: I had never ___ before, so I was excited about the trip.

items.rule: 과거 시점까지의 경험은 had + p.p.로 나타내요. fly의 p.p.는 flown이에요.

items.good: This is the best pizza I have ever eaten.
items.ko: 이것은 내가 지금까지 먹어 본 피자 중에 최고예요.
bad: This is the best pizza I have ever ate.
This is the best pizza I have ever eat.
This is the best pizza I have ever eating.

cz.st: This is the best pizza I have ever ___.

items.rule: 최상급 뒤의 'I have ever + p.p.'는 지금까지의 경험을 말해요. eat의 p.p.는 eaten이에요.

items.good: It is the first time that she has flown alone.
items.ko: 그녀가 혼자 비행기를 타는 것은 이번이 처음이에요.
bad: It is the first time that she has fly alone.
It is the first time that she is flown alone.
It is the first time that she have flown alone.

cz.st: It is the first time that she has ___ alone.

items.rule: It is the first time that ~ 뒤에는 현재완료(has/have + p.p.)가 와요.

items.good: It has been three years since I last saw my cousin.
items.ko: 내가 사촌을 마지막으로 본 지 3년이 되었어요.
bad: It has been three years since I last see my cousin.
It has been three years since I will see my cousin.
It has be three years since I last saw my cousin.

cz.st: It has been three years since I last ___ my cousin.

items.rule: It has been + 기간 + since + 과거시제 문장은 '~한 지 …가 되었다'는 뜻이에요.

items.good: The old bridge has been repaired, so you can cross it again.
items.ko: 그 오래된 다리는 수리되어서 다시 건널 수 있어요.
bad: The old bridge has repaired, so you can cross it again.
The old bridge is been repaired, so you can cross it again.
The old bridge have been repaired, so you can cross it again.

cz.st: The old bridge has been ___, so you can cross it again.

items.rule: '~되어 있다'는 현재완료 수동태 has/have been + p.p.로 나타내요.

items.good: The thief had been caught before the police arrived.
items.ko: 경찰이 도착하기 전에 도둑은 이미 붙잡혀 있었어요.
bad: The thief had caught before the police arrived.
The thief has been caught before the police arrived.
The thief had been catch before the police arrived.

cz.st: The thief had been ___ before the police arrived.

items.rule: 과거완료 수동태는 had been + p.p.예요. catch의 p.p.는 caught예요.

items.good: She had been waiting for two hours when the bus finally came.
items.ko: 버스가 마침내 왔을 때 그녀는 두 시간째 기다리고 있던 참이었어요.
bad: She has been waiting for two hours when the bus finally came.
She had been wait for two hours when the bus finally came.
She had waiting for two hours when the bus finally came.

cz.st: She had been ___ for two hours when the bus finally came.

items.rule: 과거의 어느 시점까지 계속되던 동작은 had been + -ing(과거완료진행)로 나타내요.

items.good: My hands were dirty because I had been working in the garden.
items.ko: 나는 정원에서 일하고 있었기 때문에 손이 더러웠어요.
bad: My hands were dirty because I have been working in the garden.
My hands were dirty because I had been worked in the garden.
My hands were dirty because I had working in the garden.

cz.st: My hands were dirty because I ___ been working in the garden.

items.rule: 과거의 상태(were dirty)의 원인이 된 그 이전의 계속된 동작은 had been + -ing로 나타내요.

items.good: By the end of this year, Mina will have been teaching for fifteen years.
items.ko: 올해 말이면 미나는 15년째 가르치고 있는 셈이에요.
bad: By the end of this year, Mina has been teaching for fifteen years.
By the end of this year, Mina will be taught for fifteen years.
By the end of this year, Mina will have been teach for fifteen years.

cz.st: By the end of this year, Mina will have been ___ for fifteen years.

items.rule: 미래의 한 시점까지 계속될 동작은 will have been + -ing(미래완료진행)로 나타내요.

items.good: Hardly had we sat down when the lights went out.
items.ko: 우리가 자리에 앉자마자 불이 나갔어요.
bad: Hardly we had sat down when the lights went out.
Hardly we sat down when the lights went out.
Hardly had we sit down when the lights went out.

cz.st: Hardly had we ___ down when the lights went out.

items.rule: Hardly 뒤에서는 had + 주어 + p.p. 순서로 도치되고, when이 이어져요. sit의 p.p.는 sat이에요.

items.good: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
items.ko: 나는 그렇게 아름다운 일몰을 본 적이 없어요.
bad: Never I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
Never have I saw such a beautiful sunset.
Never did I seen such a beautiful sunset.

cz.st: Never have I ___ such a beautiful sunset.

items.rule: Never가 문장 앞에 오면 have + 주어 + p.p. 순서로 도치돼요.

items.good: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
items.ko: 내가 더 열심히 공부했더라면 시험에 합격했을 거예요.
bad: If I have studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would passed the exam.
If I would have studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

cz.st: If I ___ studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

items.rule: 과거 사실의 반대는 If + had + p.p., would have + p.p.의 구조로 나타내요.

items.good: I wish I had listened to my parents.
items.ko: 부모님 말씀을 들었더라면 좋았을 텐데.
bad: I wish I have listened to my parents.
I wish I had listen to my parents.
I wish I am listened to my parents.

cz.st: I wish I ___ listened to my parents.

items.rule: 과거 일에 대한 아쉬움은 I wish + had + p.p.로 나타내요.

items.good: I will call you as soon as I have finished my work.
items.ko: 일을 끝내자마자 너에게 전화할게.
bad: I will call you as soon as I will finish my work.
I will call you as soon as I finished my work.
I will call you as soon as I will have finished my work.

cz.st: I will call you as soon as I have ___ my work.

items.rule: as soon as 같은 시간 접속사 뒤에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제나 현재완료로 써요.

items.good: Have you ever been to Gyeongju?
items.ko: 너는 경주에 가 본 적이 있니?
bad: Have you ever being to Gyeongju?
Do you ever been to Gyeongju?
Are you ever been to Gyeongju?

cz.st: Have you ever ___ to Gyeongju?

items.rule: 경험을 묻는 Have you ever + p.p.에서 be의 p.p.는 been이에요.

items.good: Mina has already sent the e-mail, so you don't have to.
items.ko: 미나가 이미 이메일을 보냈으니 너는 안 보내도 돼요.
bad: Mina has already send the e-mail, so you don't have to.
Mina is already sent the e-mail, so you don't have to.
Mina have already sent the e-mail, so you don't have to.

cz.st: Mina has already ___ the e-mail, so you don't have to.

items.rule: already는 현재완료의 has와 p.p. 사이에 놓여 '이미 끝났음'을 나타내요.

items.good: We haven't decided where to go yet.
items.ko: 우리는 어디로 갈지 아직 정하지 못했어요.
bad: We haven't decided where to go already.
We haven't decide where to go yet.
We hasn't decided where to go yet.

cz.st: We haven't decided where to go ___.

items.rule: 부정문에서 yet은 '아직 ~하지 않았다'는 뜻으로 현재완료와 함께 문장 끝에 와요.

items.good: Prices have risen sharply this year, and many families are worried.
items.ko: 올해 물가가 급격히 올라서 많은 가정이 걱정하고 있어요.
bad: Prices have rose sharply this year, and many families are worried.
Prices has risen sharply this year, and many families are worried.
Prices are risen sharply this year, and many families are worried.

cz.st: Prices have ___ sharply this year, and many families are worried.

items.rule: rise의 p.p.는 risen이에요. 주어가 복수(Prices)이므로 have를 써요.

items.good: Since moving to Seoul, she has made many new friends.
items.ko: 서울로 이사 온 이후 그녀는 새 친구를 많이 사귀었어요.
bad: Since moving to Seoul, she is making many new friends.
Since move to Seoul, she has made many new friends.
Since moving to Seoul, she has make many new friends.

cz.st: Since moving to Seoul, she has ___ many new friends.

items.rule: since 구 뒤의 주절은 현재완료를 써요. make의 p.p.는 made예요.

items.good: I had expected the test to be difficult, but it was quite easy.
items.ko: 나는 시험이 어려울 거라고 예상했었지만 꽤 쉬웠어요.
bad: I have expected the test to be difficult, but it was quite easy.
I had expect the test to be difficult, but it was quite easy.
I was expected had the test to be difficult, but it was quite easy.

cz.st: I ___ expected the test to be difficult, but it was quite easy.

items.rule: 예상한 시점이 과거의 사실(it was)보다 앞서므로 had + p.p.를 써요.

items.good: When I called, she had already gone out.
items.ko: 내가 전화했을 때 그녀는 이미 외출하고 없었어요.
bad: When I called, she has already gone out.
When I called, she was already go out.
When I called, she had already went out.

cz.st: When I called, she had already ___ out.

items.rule: go의 p.p.는 gone이에요. 과거완료에는 과거형 went를 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Because it had snowed all night, the roads were closed this morning.
items.ko: 밤새 눈이 와서 오늘 아침 도로가 통제되었어요.
bad: Because it had snowing all night, the roads were closed this morning.
Because it had been snow all night, the roads were closed this morning.
Because it was snowed all night, the roads were closed this morning.

cz.st: Because it ___ snowed all night, the roads were closed this morning.

items.rule: 과거의 결과(were closed)보다 앞선 원인은 had + p.p.로 나타내요.

items.good: Scientists have been studying the coral reef for decades.
items.ko: 과학자들은 수십 년 동안 그 산호초를 연구해 오고 있어요.
bad: Scientists are studying the coral reef for decades.
Scientists has been studying the coral reef for decades.
Scientists have being studying the coral reef for decades.

cz.st: Scientists have been ___ the coral reef for decades.

items.rule: for decades처럼 오랜 기간 계속된 동작은 have been + -ing로 나타내요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: Jun ___ the guitar for three years before he joined the school band.
items.why: 학교 밴드에 들어간 과거 시점보다 앞서 이어진 일이므로 과거완료 had played가 알맞아요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: I ___ my homework yet, so I can't go out to play.
items.why: yet과 함께 '아직 끝내지 못했다'는 현재완료 부정 haven't finished를 써요. 주어 I에는 hasn't를 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: This time next year, we ___ in our new house for six months.
items.why: 미래의 한 시점(this time next year)까지의 기간은 미래완료 will have lived로 나타내요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: When Dad came home, we ___ dinner, so he ate alone.
items.why: 아빠가 온 과거 시점보다 먼저 끝난 일이므로 과거완료 had finished를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: Ms. Kim ___ in Daegu since 2012, but she is moving to Seoul next month.
items.why: 2012년부터 지금까지 이어진 상태이므로 since와 함께 현재완료 has lived를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: How long ___ for the bus so far? It is already getting dark.
items.why: 지금까지 계속된 동작의 기간을 물을 때는 현재완료진행 have you been waiting을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: I ___ a tennis racket before, so the first lesson was hard.
items.why: 첫 수업(과거)보다 앞선 경험이 없었으므로 had never held가 알맞아요. 주어 I에는 has를 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: Which sentence about Sora's weekend is NOT correct?
o: She went to the beach last Saturday.
She has been to the beach three times this summer.
She has gone to the beach last Saturday.
She had never seen the sea before that day.
items.why: last Saturday처럼 과거의 한 시점을 나타내는 말은 현재완료와 함께 쓸 수 없어요. 과거시제 went를 써야 해요.

items.q: Which time expression usually goes with the past simple, not the present perfect?
items.why: ago는 과거의 한 시점을 나타내므로 과거시제와 쓰고, so far, up to now, in recent weeks는 현재완료와 잘 어울려요.

items.q: Which time expression is natural with the present perfect?
items.why: '이번 달 지금까지'는 아직 끝나지 않은 기간이라 현재완료와 어울려요. 나머지는 과거의 한 시점이라 과거시제를 써요.

items.q: Which expression can follow 'since' in the sentence "She has been absent since ___"?
items.why: since 뒤에는 시작 시점이 와요. three days, about two weeks, two hours는 기간이라 for와 함께 써요.

items.q: Which expression can follow 'for' in the sentence "He has been absent for ___"?
items.why: for 뒤에는 기간이 와요. Monday, last week, yesterday는 시점이라 since와 함께 써요.

items.q: Which sentence tells us that Jina has not come back yet?
o: Jina has been to the bank.
Jina had been to the bank.
Jina has never been to the bank.
Jina has gone to the bank.
items.why: has gone to는 '가고 없다'는 뜻이고, has/had been to는 다녀와서 지금은 돌아와 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: In the sentence "When the teacher came in, the students had cleaned the room," what happened first?
o: The teacher walked into the room.
items.why: had cleaned는 과거완료로 선생님이 들어온 것보다 먼저 일어난 일을 나타내요.

items.q: In the sentence "She will have finished the report by noon," when is the report finished?
items.why: by noon은 '정오까지'이고 will have finished는 그 시점까지 끝나 있을 것임을 나타내요.

items.q: Which sentence means the same as "I last visited Grandma in March"?
o: I haven't visited Grandma since March.
I haven't visited Grandma for March.
I hadn't visited Grandma since March.
I have visited Grandma twice since March.
items.why: 3월 이후로 방문하지 않았다는 뜻은 since와 현재완료 부정으로 나타내요. for 뒤에는 기간이 와요.

items.q: Which sentence means the same as "He started working here in 2018 and still works here"?
o: He will have worked here since 2018.
items.why: 2018년부터 지금까지 계속되는 일은 since와 현재완료 has worked로 나타내요.

items.q: Which sentence suggests that the rain may still be falling?
o: It will have rained all morning.
It has been raining all morning.
items.why: 현재완료진행 has been raining은 지금까지 계속된 동작을 나타내서 아직 비가 올 수 있음을 암시해요.

items.q: Which sentence uses 'ever' correctly?
o: I have ever ridden a horse.
She has ever not ridden a horse.
Have you ever ridden a horse?
They ever rode a horse yesterday.
items.why: ever는 주로 의문문이나 최상급 뒤에서 '지금까지 한 번이라도'의 뜻으로 현재완료와 함께 써요.

items.q: Choose the best word: "Have you cleaned your room ___?"
items.why: 의문문과 부정문 끝에 오는 yet은 '벌써, 아직'의 뜻으로 현재완료와 함께 써요.

items.q: Choose the best word: "We have been friends ___ we were in elementary school."
items.why: since 뒤에 시작 시점(절)이 오면 그때부터 지금까지의 계속을 나타내요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "I ___ him since last summer, so I don't know how he is."
items.why: 지난여름부터 지금까지 소식이 없으므로 since와 현재완료 부정 haven't heard from을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "The kitchen smells wonderful. Dad ___ since noon."
items.why: 정오부터 지금까지 계속된 동작은 현재완료진행 has been baking으로 나타내요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Yuna's English is much better because she ___ for the past six months."
items.why: for the past six months는 지금까지의 기간이므로 현재완료(진행)를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "By the end of the semester, we ___ all five chapters."
items.why: 학기 말이라는 미래 시점까지 끝날 일이므로 미래완료 will have covered를 써요.

items.q: Which sentence about the school festival is NOT correct?
o: We have rehearsed the play last week.
We have rehearsed the play since March.
We had rehearsed twice before the principal watched.
We will have finished the poster by Friday.
items.why: last week는 과거의 한 시점이므로 현재완료와 쓸 수 없어요. 과거시제 rehearsed를 써야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence about Hana's job is NOT correct?
o: Hana has been working here for three years.
Hana had worked here before she moved to Busan.
items.why: 2020은 시작 시점이므로 for가 아니라 since와 함께 써야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence about the weather is NOT correct?
o: It has rained for three days.
It had rained before we left.
It has been raining since Monday.
It has rained since three days.
items.why: three days는 기간이므로 since가 아니라 for와 함께 써야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence about the trip is NOT correct?
o: By the time we arrived, the shop had closed.
By the time you read this, we will have landed.
By the time we arrived, the shop will have closed.
By the end of next week, we will have seen the whole island.
items.why: arrived는 과거이므로 미래완료 will have closed와 맞지 않아요. 과거완료 had closed가 알맞아요.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence about Chulsu's lunch.
o: He has already eat his lunch.
He has already eaten his lunch.
He already has ate his lunch.
He have already eaten his lunch.
items.why: 현재완료는 has + p.p.이고 eat의 p.p.는 eaten이에요. 주어 He에는 has를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "The museum has attracted visitors since it ___ in 1998."
items.why: since 뒤의 절은 과거의 시작 시점을 나타내므로 과거시제 opened를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Scientists ___ better ways to clean seawater since the 1990s."
items.why: 1990년대부터 지금까지 이어진 일이므로 since와 현재완료 have developed를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers ___ for two days."
items.why: 구조대가 도착한 과거 시점까지 계속된 동작은 과거완료진행 had been walking으로 나타내요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Please don't leave. The meeting ___ yet."
items.why: 지금 아직 끝나지 않았다는 뜻이므로 yet과 함께 현재완료 부정 hasn't ended를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "My phone is dead because I ___ it all day."
items.why: 하루 종일 계속 써서 지금 배터리가 다 됐다는 뜻이므로 현재완료진행을 써요.

items.q: In which sentence does 'had' help form the past perfect?
o: She had a big cup of hot tea at noon.
She had finished her tea before I came.
She had to leave the party early.
She had lunch with Ben at the school café.
items.why: 정답 문장의 had는 finished와 함께 과거완료를 이루는 조동사예요. 나머지의 had는 '먹었다', '해야 했다'는 뜻의 본동사예요.

items.q: In which sentence does 'have' help form the present perfect?
o: We have visited the palace twice.
We have lunch at one o'clock every day.
items.why: 정답 문장의 have는 visited와 함께 현재완료를 이루는 조동사예요. 나머지의 have는 본동사예요.

items.q: Which sentence describes an action that began in the past and is still going on?
o: Dad worked at the bank until 2015.
Dad had worked at the bank before he retired.
Dad did not work at the bank last year.
Dad has worked at the bank for ten years.
items.why: 현재완료는 과거에 시작해 지금까지 이어지는 일을 나타내요. 나머지는 이미 끝난 일이에요.

items.q: Which sentence describes an action completed before another past action?
o: I ate dinner while she was calling.
I am eating when she calls.
I had eaten before she called.
I will eat before she calls.
items.why: had eaten은 전화가 온 과거 시점보다 먼저 끝난 일을 나타내요.

items.q: "They had been arguing for an hour when the teacher walked in." What was happening when the teacher walked in?
o: They stopped arguing an hour earlier.
The argument had already lasted an hour.
They began to argue after the teacher left.
items.why: had been arguing for an hour는 선생님이 들어온 시점까지 한 시간 동안 다툼이 계속되었다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Which sentence shows a past event that still affects the present?
o: I lost my keys in 2015, and I found them a week later.
I have lost my keys, so I can't open the door.
I lost my keys last year, but I found them soon after.
I had lost my keys before I was ten years old.
items.why: 현재완료는 과거의 일이 지금까지 영향을 줄 때 써요. 나머지는 과거에 이미 끝난 일이에요.

items.q: Which question asks about a person's experience?
o: Have you ever flown in a helicopter?
Will you fly in a helicopter next week?
Are you flying in a helicopter now?
What time did the helicopter leave?
items.why: Have you ever + p.p.?는 지금까지의 경험을 묻는 표현이에요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "I ___ you for ages! Where have you been?"
items.why: 오랫동안 못 본 것이 지금까지 이어지므로 현재완료 부정 haven't seen을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Sam ___ his speech by the time the guests arrive tonight."
items.why: 오늘 밤 손님이 도착할 미래 시점까지 끝낼 일이므로 미래완료 will have finished를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Hyunwoo is exhausted. He ___ since five this morning."
items.why: 아침 다섯 시부터 지금까지 계속 일해서 지쳤다는 뜻이므로 현재완료진행을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "We couldn't get in because we ___ our tickets at home."
items.why: 들어가지 못한 과거 시점보다 앞서 티켓을 두고 온 것이므로 과거완료 had left를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "After the storm ___, the villagers began to repair the roofs."
items.why: 마을 사람들이 수리를 시작한 과거 시점보다 먼저 폭풍이 지나갔으므로 과거완료를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Many things have changed since I ___ elementary school."
items.why: since 뒤의 절은 과거의 시작 시점을 나타내므로 과거시제 left를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Wow, your English is excellent! How long ___ it?"
items.why: 지금까지 계속해 온 기간을 물을 때 현재완료진행 have you been studying을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "I'm sorry I'm late. I ___ for a taxi for twenty minutes!"
items.why: 20분 동안 계속 기다렸다는 뜻이므로 for와 함께 현재완료진행을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "This is the third time the printer ___ this week."
items.why: This is the third time that 뒤에는 현재완료를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "By 2050, many cities ___ their old buses with electric ones."
items.why: 2050년이라는 미래 시점까지 완료될 일이므로 미래완료 will have replaced를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Mr. Choi ___ the marathon three times, so he knows the route well."
items.why: 경험의 횟수를 말하는 현재완료이고 run의 p.p.는 run이에요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Haeun ___ sushi until she visited Tokyo."
items.why: 도쿄를 방문한 과거 시점까지의 경험이 없었다는 뜻이므로 과거완료 had never tried를 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Have you ___ the news about the school trip?"
items.why: 현재완료 have + 주어 + p.p.에서 hear의 p.p.는 heard예요.

items.q: Choose the best answer. A: Is Dad home? B: No, he ___ to the market. He'll be back soon.
items.why: 아직 돌아오지 않았다는 뜻이므로 has gone을 써요. has been to는 다녀온 경험을 나타내요.

items.q: Choose the best answer. A: Have you tried the new café? B: Yes, I ___ there twice.
items.why: 경험을 대답할 때는 현재완료 have been을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: "Sumin ___ three e-mails to the manager since this morning, but nobody has answered."
items.why: 오늘 아침부터 지금까지의 일이므로 since와 현재완료 has sent를 써요.

items.title: A Late Start
items.text: Hana woke up at nine, and she knew at once that something was wrong. Her alarm clock had stopped during the night because its battery had died. By the time she reached the bus stop, the school bus had already left. She had been looking forward to the science fair for weeks, and she had worked on her project until midnight the night before. Now she was going to miss the opening ceremony. Luckily, her neighbor, Mr. Yoon, saw her running down the street and offered her a ride. When they pulled up at the school gate, the ceremony had just begun, and Hana slipped quietly into the hall.

qs.q: Why did Hana wake up late?
o: Her alarm clock's battery had died.
She had worked on her project until sunrise.
Her neighbor had forgotten to wake her.
She had mistaken the date of the fair.
qs.why: 본문에서 알람 시계가 밤사이 멈췄고 배터리가 다 되었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What had already happened when Hana reached the bus stop?
o: The science fair had been cancelled.
qs.why: By the time she reached the bus stop, the school bus had already left라고 했어요.

qs.q: What can we infer about Hana?
o: She often forgets to set her alarm.
She did not trust her neighbor.
She cared about the science fair.
qs.why: 몇 주 동안 과학 박람회를 기대했고 자정까지 준비했다는 데서 박람회를 소중히 여겼음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "slipped quietly into" is closest in meaning to ...
o: fell down on the wet floor inside
left the hall in a hurry
qs.why: slip into는 여기서 조용히 눈에 띄지 않게 들어갔다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which event happened last?
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 학교에 도착한 뒤 Hana가 강당에 조용히 들어갔어요.

items.title: Greetings from Seoul
items.text: Dear Mom and Dad, I have been in Seoul for two weeks now, and I wanted to write before I forget everything! I have already visited three palaces, and I have tried more Korean dishes than I can count. My favorite so far is bibimbap, although I haven't learned to use chopsticks properly yet. My teacher says my Korean has improved a lot since I arrived, but I still make plenty of mistakes. I have also made a few friends at school, and one of them has invited me to her grandmother's house this weekend. I haven't felt homesick at all, but I do miss our garden. Please say hello to Max for me. Love, Laura

qs.q: Why did Laura write this e-mail?
o: To tell her parents about her time in Seoul
To ask her parents to send some Korean snacks
To complain about her new classes at school
To invite her parents to visit her in Seoul soon
qs.why: 편지는 서울에서 지낸 첫 두 주의 경험을 부모님께 알리는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Which food does Laura like best so far?
qs.why: My favorite so far is bibimbap이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "homesick" mean in the e-mail?
o: Sick because of the unfamiliar food
Sad because you miss your home
qs.why: homesick은 집이 그리워서 마음이 힘든 상태를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What can we infer about Laura's Korean?
o: It was already perfect when she first arrived here.
It is better than before, but not perfect.
It has not changed since she came.
It is worse than her cooking skills.
qs.why: 선생님이 많이 늘었다고 했지만 여전히 실수가 많다고 했어요.

qs.q: Who has invited Laura to a grandmother's house?
qs.why: one of them(학교에서 사귄 친구들 중 한 명)이 초대했어요.

items.title: Sorting It Out
items.text: Since the recycling project began in March, students at Hanbit High School have collected more than 4,000 plastic bottles. Before the project started, the school had thrown away almost everything in a single bin. Now each classroom has three labeled bins, and a team of volunteers has been checking them every Friday. According to the project leader, Jiho, the amount of garbage has dropped by nearly a third. However, not everyone is satisfied. Some teachers say the volunteers have been missing class to finish their rounds. The student council has promised to find a solution by the end of next month, and by then the school will have recycled enough bottles to fill a small truck.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A teacher's plan to cancel Friday classes
A student council election at Hanbit High School
A school recycling project and its results
A truck that carries bottles to a factory
qs.why: 학교의 재활용 프로젝트와 그 결과, 문제점을 다루고 있어요.

qs.q: What did the school do with its garbage before the project?
o: It sorted it into three labeled bins.
It threw almost all of it into one bin.
It sold most of it to a recycling company.
It asked students to take it home.
qs.why: Before the project started, the school had thrown away almost everything in a single bin이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Which statement about the volunteers is true?
o: They check the bins once a week.
They are paid by the student council.
They work only during lunch time.
They have refused to join the project.
qs.why: 해당 팀이 매주 금요일마다 분리수거함을 확인한다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why are some teachers unhappy?
o: Students have thrown away too many bottles.
The bins take up too much space in classrooms.
Jiho has spoken against the project.
Volunteers sometimes miss class to finish their rounds.
qs.why: 일부 교사는 자원봉사자들이 순회를 마치느라 수업을 빠진다고 말했어요.

items.title: My Year on the Ice
items.text: I had never been on ice skates until last winter, and my first lesson was a disaster. I had practiced walking on the ice for ten minutes when I fell and landed on my back. My instructor, Ms. Park, laughed kindly and said every skater had fallen hundreds of times. Since then, I have been going to the rink every Saturday. I have learned how to stop, and I have even managed to skate backward for a few seconds. Last week, a boy who had been watching me asked if I was a professional. I said no, but I couldn't stop smiling for the rest of the day. Next month, I will have been skating for a full year, and I plan to enter the beginners' show.

qs.q: What happened during the writer's first lesson?
o: The writer skated backward for a few seconds.
The writer won a small prize.
The writer fell down on the ice.
The writer met a professional skater.
qs.why: 첫 수업에서 10분간 걷는 연습을 하다가 넘어졌어요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel about skating now?
qs.why: 계속 연습해 왔고 칭찬에 하루 종일 웃었으며 쇼에도 나갈 계획이라 뿌듯하고 의욕적이에요.

qs.q: What had the boy been doing before he asked his question?
o: Practicing hard for the beginners' show
qs.why: a boy who had been watching me라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "managed to" suggest in the passage?
o: The writer was asked to teach others.
The writer tried but did not succeed.
The writer was in charge of the rink.
The writer succeeded in doing something difficult.
qs.why: manage to는 어려운 일을 해내다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer plan to do?
o: Take a break for a year
Buy a new pair of skates
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 beginners' show에 참가할 계획이라고 했어요.

items.title: Dear Sunny
items.text: Dear Sunny, I have been feeling exhausted for weeks. I have tried going to bed earlier, but nothing has changed. Last month I had been staying up late to study, and I thought that was the cause. Now I sleep eight hours, yet I still wake up tired. What should I do? Sleepy in Daejeon. Dear Sleepy, Thank you for writing. Many students have faced the same problem. Your body may still be recovering from the weeks when you had been sleeping too little. It can take a while to pay back that sleep debt. In the meantime, I suggest you avoid screens before bed. If you haven't felt better by the end of the month, please see a doctor.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of Sunny's reply?
o: To explain how to study for exams
To give a reader some advice
qs.why: 독자의 피로 문제에 조언을 해 주는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does the word "that" in "I thought that was the cause" refer to?
o: Going to bed earlier than usual
qs.why: that은 앞에서 말한 늦게까지 공부하느라 깨어 있던 것을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What does Sunny mean by "sleep debt"?
o: Sleep that must be made up
Money paid for a sleeping room
A habit of sleeping too much
The time needed to fall asleep
qs.why: sleep debt는 부족했던 잠을 나중에 보충해야 하는 것을 비유하는 말이에요.

qs.q: According to the reply, when should the writer visit a doctor?
o: Right after the writer finishes reading this reply letter
After sleeping ten hours a night for a whole week
Before going to bed on every day of the month
If she has not improved by the end of the month
qs.why: If you haven't felt better by the end of the month, please see a doctor라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why might the writer still feel tired?
o: The writer is sleeping far too many hours now.
The writer has stopped studying for exams completely.
The body may still be catching up on lost sleep.
The writer drinks too little water during the day.
qs.why: 이전 몇 주간 잠이 부족했던 상태에서 몸이 아직 회복 중일 수 있다고 했어요.

items.title: The Light on the Rocks
items.text: Cape Willow Lighthouse was built in 1884, after a storm had destroyed three ships near the rocks. For almost a century, a keeper lived in the tower and lit the lamp every evening. By 1975, however, the lighthouse had been replaced by an automatic light, and the last keeper had moved away. The empty tower slowly fell into disrepair until local volunteers began to fix it in 2008. They have been working on it ever since. So far, they have painted the walls, replaced the stairs, and reopened the lamp room to visitors. By next summer, they hope to have raised enough money to restore the original lens, which has been stored in a museum for fifty years.

qs.q: Why was Cape Willow Lighthouse built?
o: A famous keeper wanted a new home near the sea.
The town needed a place for visitors to enjoy the view.
Ships had been destroyed in a storm near the rocks.
An automatic light had stopped working near the rocks.
qs.why: 폭풍이 근처 바위에서 배 세 척을 부순 뒤에 지어졌어요.

qs.q: What had happened by 1975?
o: The tower had been opened to visitors.
An automatic light had taken over.
The volunteers had finished repairing the stairs.
The original lens had returned to the tower.
qs.why: By 1975 the lighthouse had been replaced by an automatic light라고 했어요.

qs.q: What have the volunteers done so far?
o: Restored the original lens and lamp
Built a new museum for the old lens
Hired a new keeper for the tower
qs.why: So far 뒤에 벽을 칠하고 계단을 교체하고 램프실을 열었다고 나와요.

qs.q: In the passage, "disrepair" most likely means ...
qs.why: 탑이 비어 있어서 서서히 낡아 갔다는 흐름이므로 수리가 안 된 나쁜 상태를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What can we infer about the original lens?
o: It was destroyed by the storm.
It was sold to a private collector.
It has not been in the lighthouse for a long time.
It is still being used every evening.
qs.why: 렌즈가 50년 동안 박물관에 보관되어 있다는 데서 오랫동안 등대에 없었음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Reading Challenge Update
items.text: Our school's reading challenge ends on December 15. So far, 212 students have joined, and together they have read 1,340 books. Mr. Seo's class is in first place; they have finished 190 books, and they haven't missed a single week. Last year, only 150 students had signed up by this time, so this year is already a success. If every student keeps reading at the current speed, we will have passed 2,000 books by the final day. Prizes will be given to the top three classes at the closing ceremony. Remember to write down each book you finish on the sheet outside the library.

qs.q: Which class is in first place now?
qs.why: Mr. Seo's class is in first place라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the comparison with last year show?
o: Fewer books were read last year.
The challenge was cancelled last year.
More students are joining this year.
qs.why: 작년 이맘때는 150명이 신청했는데 올해는 212명이라 참여 학생이 늘었어요.

qs.q: What will happen if students keep reading at the current speed?
o: Mr. Seo's class will lose first place.
The library will close for repairs.
qs.why: If every student keeps reading at the current speed, we will have passed 2,000 books라고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last sentence?
o: To announce the winners of the prizes
To tell students how to record their books
To warn students about late books
To explain why the library is closed
qs.why: 마지막 문장은 읽은 책을 도서관 밖 용지에 기록하라고 안내해요.

items.title: The Box in the Attic
items.text: When Eun-seo cleaned out her grandmother's attic, she found a small wooden box. Inside was a letter that had been written seventy years earlier. The paper had turned yellow, but the handwriting was still clear. The letter was from her grandfather, who had been working far from home at the time. He wrote that he had saved enough money to buy a small piece of land, and that he would return before spring. Eun-seo had never known that her grandparents had been separated for so long. She hurried downstairs and showed the letter to her grandmother, who read it slowly and then smiled with tears in her eyes. "I had forgotten that I kept this," she whispered.

qs.q: Where did Eun-seo find the letter?
o: In a box in the attic
In a drawer in the kitchen
In a book at the library
qs.why: She found a small wooden box in her grandmother's attic이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why had the grandfather been away from home?
o: He had been looking for his lost box.
He had been visiting a friend.
He had been working far away.
qs.why: the grandfather, who had been working far from home이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What had Eun-seo not known before?
o: Her grandmother kept a diary of her whole life.
Her grandfather owned a farm outside the city.
Her grandparents had lived apart for so long.
The attic held boxes of old family photographs.
qs.why: Eun-seo had never known that her grandparents had been separated for so long이라고 했어요.

qs.q: How did the grandmother probably feel when she read the letter?
qs.why: 눈물을 글썽이며 미소 지었다는 데서 감동했음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Third Time Lucky
items.text: I have been to Maple Corner Café three times, and each visit has been better than the last. When I first went in September, the café had only just opened, and my coffee was a little cold. By my second visit, however, the staff had fixed the problem and even added a quiet reading room upstairs. Last weekend, I stayed for almost four hours without realizing it. I have tried most of the desserts, and the apple tart is the best I have ever eaten. The only complaint I have is the price, which has risen twice since the café opened. Still, I would recommend it to anyone who has been looking for a calm place to study.

qs.q: What is the writer's overall opinion of the café?
o: Negative, with a few good points
Angry, because of the cold coffee
qs.why: 전반적으로 칭찬하는 글이고 가격만 아쉬운 점으로 꼽았어요.

qs.q: What had the staff done by the writer's second visit?
o: Lowered the prices of all the desserts
Closed the café for several weeks of repairs
Hired a new baker to make the apple tart
Fixed the coffee problem and added a reading room
qs.why: By my second visit, the staff had fixed the problem and even added a quiet reading room이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the writer's one complaint?
o: The reading room is too noisy.
The price has gone up twice.
The apple tart is too sweet.
qs.why: The only complaint I have is the price라고 했어요.

qs.q: Who would the writer recommend the café to?
qs.why: calm place to study를 찾는 사람에게 추천한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can we infer about the writer's last visit to the café?
o: The writer was waiting for a friend who arrived late.
The writer felt relaxed and lost track of time.
The writer left early because the room was too noisy.
The writer was upset about the high prices that day.
qs.why: 거의 네 시간 동안 머물렀는데도 몰랐다는 데서 편안하게 시간을 보냈음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: A Word from Coach Han
items.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I have been coaching this team for six years, and I have seen many players come and go. Before I started, this club had never won a regional title. Since then, we have won it twice. But trophies are not what I remember most. I remember a boy who had been sitting on the bench for two seasons without playing a single minute. He had never complained. When he finally got his chance, he scored in the first five minutes. What had changed? Nothing, except that he had never stopped practicing. By the end of this season, some of you will have played together for four years. Please remember that patience has made this team strong.

qs.q: What is the main message of the talk?
o: Winning trophies is the only goal.
Patience and steady effort lead to success.
The coach plans to leave the club.
qs.why: 벤치에 있으면서도 연습을 멈추지 않은 소년의 이야기로 인내와 꾸준함을 강조해요.

qs.q: How many regional titles has the team won since the coach arrived?
qs.why: Since then, we have won it twice라고 했어요.

qs.q: What had the boy done while sitting on the bench?
o: He had asked to change teams.
He had complained to the coach.
He had stopped coming to practice.
qs.why: he had never stopped practicing이라고 했어요.

qs.q: When did the boy score?
o: During his first season on the bench
Soon after he finally got his chance
At the end of his four years
After the coach left the club
qs.why: When he finally got his chance, he scored in the first five minutes라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "come and go" mean in "I have seen many players come and go"?
o: Win some matches and lose others
Join the team and later leave it
Get hurt and then recover quickly
qs.why: come and go는 왔다가 떠난다는 뜻으로, 많은 선수가 팀에 들어왔다가 떠났다는 의미예요.

items.title: Bikes Around Greenfield
items.text: Greenfield's bike-sharing program has grown quickly since it began two years ago. At first, the city had provided only fifty bikes at five stations. Today, there are four hundred bikes at forty stations, and residents have made more than a million trips. The program has also reduced traffic; officials say that car use in the center has fallen by about eight percent. However, some bikes have been damaged, and the city has been looking for ways to prevent it. Next year, new stations will open near the river, and by then the city will have added another hundred bikes. Citizens may send suggestions to the city office.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A plan to ban cars in the center
qs.why: 자전거 공유 프로그램의 성장과 효과, 앞으로의 계획을 다뤄요.

qs.q: How many bikes did the program begin with?
qs.why: At first, the city had provided only fifty bikes라고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the city trying to prevent?
qs.why: 일부 자전거가 파손되어 이를 막을 방법을 찾고 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can we infer from the passage about car use?
o: It has gone down since the program began.
It has doubled in the center.
It has not changed at all.
It is now banned near the river.
qs.why: 도심의 자동차 이용이 약 8퍼센트 줄었다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "residents" means ...
o: people who live in a place
qs.why: residents는 그 지역에 사는 주민을 뜻해요.

items.ko: 최근에
items.ex: I have been feeling tired lately.

items.ko: 이전에
items.ex: The hotel, previously a school, opened last spring.
items.exko: 예전에 학교였던 그 호텔은 지난봄에 문을 열었어요.

items.ko: 결국, 마침내
items.ex: After many failed attempts, she eventually passed the test.
items.exko: 여러 번 실패한 끝에 그녀는 마침내 시험에 합격했어요.

items.ko: 지금까지
items.ex: How many pages have you read so far?
